output.methodChoice: Kepner-Tregoe specification (IS/IS NOT) on the drop, then competing-hypotheses comparison, plus a source-provenance check on the interested parties' claims.
output.brief:
The drop is almost certainly not caused by Android 6.14. On 3 March at 10:38 UTC, Corvane's automatic rule-pack update added a rule (AUTO-LIB-17). It blocks password-login requests from the nettle-http library, which every Android app version uses. About 9,600 requests a day are blocked with a 403. The blocked requests come from about 41,300 install IDs, 92% of which logged in successfully in the previous 90 days, so they look like real customers rather than bots. The failures began within a minute on every app version, including 6.11 and older. They appear equally with and without the March OS patch. Quick-unlock, iOS and web are unaffected. Password success on Android fell from 96% to 8%.

What to do: don't roll back 6.14, and don't raise bot sensitivity. Raising it would block more real customers. Don't exclude blocked attempts from the KPI, because that would hide a real customer-facing failure. Instead, ask Corvane to put the rules added in 2026.03.1 into log-only mode on the mobile password path, keeping rate limits, lockout and other rules active. Then confirm in telemetry that password success returns to about 96%. Remaining uncertainty: the contact-centre call rise is only loosely tied to the login failures.
